summary.en: Attach values and environments to grammar symbols, then evaluate an annotated expression tree in Python.
summary.bn: গ্রামারের সঙ্গে মান আর স্কোপের তথ্য জুড়ে তুমি এক্সপ্রেশনের ফল বের করতে পারবে।

notes: Python programs use the standard library and were executed with Python 3.12.14.

examples.title: Evaluate a synthesised expression value
examples.explanationHtml: The multiplication subtree contributes 20; the root adds 3 to produce 23.

examples.title: List postorder value annotations
examples.explanationHtml: The inner addition has value 7, which multiplication combines with 5.

examples.title: Pass an identifier environment
examples.explanationHtml: The name leaf reads 40 from its environment and the expression becomes 50.

practice.title: Evaluate an integer expression
practice.statementHtml: Read one expression of at most 100 characters, with ASCII integers, +, -, *, unary minus and parentheses. Print Expression:, then its integer value. Print invalid for syntax errors, unknown names or unsupported characters. Limit nesting to 30.
hints: Parse before evaluating; the AST records precedence.

practice.title: Print postorder attributes
practice.statementHtml: Read a numeric expression using the same operators, at most 80 characters and 20 nested operations. Print Expression to annotate:, then one postorder row operation text: value. Leaves use number and their literal text; other nodes use their operator (neg for unary minus) and a dash. On a malformed expression or name, print invalid.
hints: Visit children before recording their parent.

practice.title: Declaration attributes
practice.statementHtml: Give inherited type attributes for real fee, tax using D → Type Names.
practice.answerHtml:
Consider D → Type Names and Names → id Rest. The declaration real fee, tax gives both names type real. Type.type is synthesised from the keyword. D passes it down as Names.in, and the names list carries it from left to right.

Inherited type information
OccurrenceAttribute equationValue for real fee, tax
TypeType.type = realreal
NamesNames.in = Type.typereal
id feeinstall(fee, Names.in)fee: real
RestRest.in = Names.inreal
id taxinstall(tax, Rest.in)tax: real

An L-attributed definition allows inherited attributes of a right-side occurrence to depend on the parent's inherited attributes and earlier right-side occurrences. Synthesised values still travel upwards. This supports a left-to-right depth-first evaluation when the full dependency graph is acyclic. Every S-attributed definition is also L-attributed.

For A → B C, assigning B.in = C.val requires a later sibling. That equation violates the usual L-attributed restriction. You might evaluate C first using a general dependency schedule, but a straightforward left-to-right visit cannot supply B.in in time. Do not call a definition L-attributed merely because it has inherited attributes.

practice.title: Dependency diagnosis
practice.statementHtml: Compare child-to-parent, later-sibling and cyclic attribute dependencies.
hints: Draw an arrow from each prerequisite to its user.
practice.answerHtml:
Suppose A.x = B.y + 1 and B.y = A.x + 1 for the same parent-child pair. Neither value has a starting point. Drawing arrows gives A.x → B.y → A.x. There is no topological evaluation order for these equations.

Dependency review
DefinitionDependency edgesEvaluation result
E.val = T.valT.val → E.valChild before parent
Names.in = Type.typeType.type → Names.inType before names
B.in = C.val in A → B CC.val → B.inAcyclic but not L-attributed
A.x = B.y + 1; B.y = A.x + 1A.x ↔ B.yCircular; reject this evaluator

A dependency graph has one vertex per attribute occurrence, not merely one vertex per attribute name. Otherwise separate E.val occurrences would collapse and create false cycles. This distinction is especially useful when you explain an annotated tree in an exam.

quiz.prompt: Which direction supplies a synthesised E.val?
quiz.explanation: An E parent combines values already attached to its children.

quiz.prompt: What does a name leaf need besides its spelling?
quiz.explanation: The environment maps the name to the meaning visible in this context.

options: Every definition with a later-sibling dependency
quiz.explanation: S-attributed rules introduce no inherited dependency that violates the left-to-right restriction.

quiz.prompt: What is one vertex in an attribute dependency graph?
options: One nonterminal name for the entire grammar
quiz.explanation: Separate occurrences can hold different values and must remain distinct.

quiz.prompt: Why does B.in = C.val violate L-attribution in A → B C?
quiz.explanation: B needs information that a left-to-right traversal has not computed yet.

quiz.prompt: Why may an AST omit parentheses?
options: Multiplication always comes first even inside parentheses
quiz.explanation: Grouping remains in the tree structure, although punctuation leaves disappear.

quiz.prompt: When can a bottom-up parser evaluate an S-attributed reduction?
options: After the right side is recognised
quiz.explanation: The reduction has the right-side semantic values available on the parser stack.

quiz.prompt: A child product reaches the root addition. Which value is printed?
quiz.explanation: The product is 20, so the parent adds 3.

quiz.prompt: Both inherited names receive real. Which type reaches tax?
quiz.explanation: The names list forwards the same declaration type.

quiz.prompt: These synthesised child values are combined at the parent. What is its value?
quiz.explanation: The addition child is 7 before multiplication combines it with 5.

keyPoints.en: Synthesised values flow from children towards their parent.
keyPoints.bn: চাইল্ড নোডের মান থেকে প্যারেন্টের মান বের করো।

keyPoints.en: Inherited attributes carry context into a subtree.
keyPoints.bn: সাবট্রিতে স্কোপের মতো দরকারি তথ্য পাঠাতে inherited attribute লাগে।

keyPoints.en: An S-attributed definition uses only synthesised attributes.
keyPoints.bn: সব অ্যাট্রিবিউট নিচ থেকে ওপরে এলে সেটি S-attributed।

keyPoints.en: L-attributed rules restrict dependencies on later siblings.
keyPoints.bn: L-attributed নিয়মে পরের sibling-এর মান আগে চাওয়া যায় না।

keyPoints.en: A dependency cycle prevents an ordinary evaluation schedule.
keyPoints.bn: নির্ভরতার চক্র থাকলে কোন মান আগে বের করবে, তা ঠিক করা যায় না।

examQuestions.question: Annotate the parse tree and evaluate 3 + 4 * 5.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
For 3 + 4 * 5, multiplication groups inside T. Give every leaf its numeric value first. Then calculate each parent only after its dependencies are ready. The annotated tree has the same shape as the parse tree; the annotations add information without changing the grammar.

E.val=23
├── E.val=3 → T.val=3 → F.val=3 → number.lexval=3
├── +
└── T.val=20
    ├── T.val=4 → F.val=4 → number.lexval=4
    ├── *
    └── F.val=5 → number.lexval=5
One valid evaluation schedule
StepReady occurrenceCalculationResult
1Left F, T, EPass number 3 upwards3
2Inner left F and TPass number 4 upwards4
3Right FRead number 55
4Multiplication T4 * 520
5Root E3 + 2023

The leftmost leaf need not be evaluated first for this pure expression. Any order that respects dependencies gives 23. However, a language with function calls or other effects may prescribe an evaluation order. An attribute equation does not give permission to reorder those effects.
